summary:
Isole's evidence is dominated by Sicily. In April 2025 three young men were beaten in a Catania fast-food restaurant at roughly 5 a.m. solely because they were gay; the victims were hospitalised, video of the attack later circulated publicly, and the prosecutor's office reconstructed the sequence (insults and threats, then the physical assault). In July 2025 a mother was attacked in Catania in an incident named in a national statement accusing the national government of "exposing us to violence". A June 2026 survey of Sicilian reporting describes a sustained pattern of rising homophobic bullying, violence against the LGBTQIA+ community and associated suicides, listing multiple cases — a patterned finding, not a single incident. Favignana (Trapani) has also hosted a national Pride-circuit march, showing visibility persists alongside the harm. No Sardinia-specific evidence was found.

Sicily is not among the six highest-victim regions in the quantitative study, but the qualitative pattern — multiple cases, suicides, a hospitalisation-level assault in a tourist-accessible city — indicates a severity profile that elevates real risk for a visitor in nightlife and public-street settings. Neither special-statute island (Sicilia, Sardegna) has used expanded legislative competence against transgender people. The violence is criminal, not state-enforced.

sources.summary: National TV news chronicle (August 2025): the Catania fast-food homophobic beating of three gay men on 26 April 2025 — victims hospitalised; the reconstruction of insults, threats and the assault from circulated video, and the prosecutors' sequence, are set out case by case.

Regional news survey (June 2026) of homophobia in Sicily: lists multiple cases of rising homophobic bullying, violence against LGBTQIA+ people and associated suicides across the island — the sustained-pattern finding for the region.

National LGBT association statement (2025 Pride circuit day, seven marches including Favignana/Trapani and Catania): names the attack on a mother in Catania and declares the government "exposing us to violence", while recording continuing Pride presence in western Sicily.
